reply_text:
Gist: The note is written: in all six cases the requirement was accepted, usually by recording it as a ruling, and no reply asked where the cascades that G compares would come from.

It is at `futon3c/TN-G-over-cascades-revisited.md` (commit e7fe9142).

**The six cases**

| Date | Seat | What the reply did | Asked where the cascades come from? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 Aug | claude-15 | Typed the idea and wrote five questions about what a policy and the preference are | No |
| 2 Sep | claude-1 | Recorded the ruling, reopened nine worklist rows, restarted the loop | No; no questions at all |
| 12 Sep | claude-15 | Recorded a ruling and dispatched an audit of Lean attestations | Partly: mentions "candidate cascades", not how they are generated |
| 15 Sep | codex-26 | Said G must not be "supplied as an arbitrary scoring function" | No; says nothing of the policy set |
| 17 Sep | claude-4 | Noted "an action can be dressed up as a one-step cascade" | Closest; but checks where the number came from, not the cascade set |
| 18 Sep | claude-12 | Surveyed the Lean against your three purposes | No; names the preference as "the one free preference constant in the census" |

**What I take from them**
- **Acceptance meant recording.** Four of six replies contain no question. Writing a ruling into a record showed it was heard, not that it could be carried out.
- **Free inputs were found one at a time.** Three different seats each found one: the scoring function, the action dressed as a cascade, the preference. Nobody went on to list them all.
- **A census of free constants already existed on 18 September** and the policy set was not in it. Its scope was constants, not collections the runtime supplies. I think this is the most specific finding.
- **Each seat met the requirement as new.** Six statements went to five seats; no reply refers to an earlier statement made to another seat.
- **No reply said it was hard or underspecified.**

**Limits**
- One search pattern, so six is a lower bound.
- I read only the immediate reply, not later turns of those sessions.
- The corpus starts on 22 August.
- Six cases give no rate.
- The "one design, no alternatives" row of the mirror is not tested.

The note ends with four things that would have changed the outcome, none built, and three follow-ups. The cheapest follow-up is repeating this for a second requirement, such as "no facades", to see whether the pattern is particular to this one.
